The dataset is provided by Goldwind Inc, one of the world's largest wind turbine manufacturers.
The raw SCADA data is collected every 7 seconds from hundreds of pre-installed sensors on wind turbines.
The dataset includes 26 continuous variables relevant to frozen blades from 3 wind turbines, with a total of 1330 hours of monitoring data.
In the semi-supervised setting, the training set includes 671 normal fragments, while the validation set includes 169 normal and 139 abnormal fragments.
In the supervised setting, the training set includes 671 normal and 550 abnormal fragments, with additional augmentation to balance the dataset.
WaveletAE outperforms the LSTM encoder-decoder and FCNN baselines in both semi-supervised and supervised settings.
In the semi-supervised setting, WaveletAE achieves an accuracy of 0.493, precision of 0.471, recall of 0.986, and F1 score of 0.637.
In the supervised setting, WaveletAE achieves an accuracy of 0.873, precision of 0.857, recall of 0.863, and F1 score of 0.861.
The sliding window voting schema in the case study allows WaveletAE to make more robust real-time predictions, with the voting threshold τ determining the balance between precision and recall.
Increasing the voting threshold τ from 0.1 to 0.9 leads to a decrease in recall from 1.0 to 0.394, while precision increases from 0.569 to 0.979.
The case study simulates a real-time setting by fetching signal blocks every 112 seconds and accumulating predictions in a sliding window.
Traditional physical sensor-based icing detection methods are limited by high costs, energy consumption, and the need for mechanical changes to wind turbines.
Icing conditions can cause up to 25% annual energy production losses for wind farms, making early detection crucial.
Ice accumulation on wind turbine blades can degrade aerodynamic performance, cause measurement errors, and lead to mechanical and electrical failures.
The wavelet detail coefficients used in WaveletAE reveal the signal variance at multiple scales, providing information in both time and frequency domains.
